# Background

# Imputations

## Administrations

For clinical studies that include multiple-dose treatment administrations,
series of administrations are often collated to single data records in the EX
domain. Such entries contain a start day and time (EXSTDTC) and an end day and
time (EXENDTC), and it is implicitly assumed that within treatment episodes, the 
drug dose, regimen, dosing frequency and time of administration remains
the same.

To make downstream analysis easier, the `add_admimnistration()` function
converts treatment administration episodes to individual administration events.
During this conversion, it is the baseline assumption that the administration
times within an episode are constant for all administration days.

Real-life EX data are often not unambiguous or have missing elements. Typical
examples include:

* missing EXENDTC in the last administration episode for a subject, e.g., for
interim data from clinical studies that are still ongoing

* missing EXENDTC for other episodes, e.g., when patient records are incomplete

* missing time of the day in EXSTDTC or EXENDTC

* EXSTDTC that conflict with the records of PCRFTDTC (the administration
reference time point for PK observations) falling into the respective episode

* in some cases, both the time of the day in EXSTDTC or EXENDTC within the EX
domain, as well as in PCRFTDTC may be missing, providing no information
on the actual administration time point apart from the nominal sampling time 
recorded in PCTPT or TPTPTNUM

In such cases, the data analyst must make certain assumptions regarding the
administration times, i.e., impute missing data. This is often more of an art
than science. There may be certain preferences stipulated by the analysis plan
that can vary between studies.

While some conflicts cannot be automatically resolved and need manual
imputations by the data programmer, the nif package provides methods to deal
with time imputations in the generation of administration events.

## Observations

```{r echo=FALSE}
grViz("
digraph surveillance_diagram {

  graph [
    layout = dot,
    rankdir = TB,
    fontsize = 10
  ]
  
  node [
    shape = rectangle,
    #fixedsize = true,
    width = 2
  ]
  
  domain [label = \"XX domain\"]
  coding_table [label = \"apply coding table\n(if applicable)\"]
  obs_filter [label = \"apply observation filter\n(if applicable)\"]
  cat_filter [label = \"apply cat/scat filters\n(if applicable)\"]
  obs_raw [shape = none, label = \"obs_raw()\"]
  merge [label = \"merge observations\ninto nif object\"]
  times [label = \"update TIME, TAD,\nTAFD fields\"]
  obs_final [shape = none, label = \"obs_final()\"]
  
  domain -> coding_table
  coding_table -> obs_filter
  obs_filter -> cat_filter
  cat_filter -> obs_raw
  obs_raw -> merge
  merge -> times
  times -> obs_final
}
")
```
